top_strength: The pricing-and-clock block was clean and confident. He opened with 'our price is super simple,' gave the day-of-week context ('Saturday, that is our highest volume day'), the $111 per mover per hour, the $222 two-man math, and everything included — gas, truck, taxes, insurance, blankets, tools for disassembly. He then ran the full clock correctly: time starts when the guys show up and start working, two-and-a-half hour minimum, fifteen-minute increments after that, and he sense-checked it ('Do you have any questions about that?'), getting 'that makes sense' back. He also translated the range into real dollars — $555 at the low end, $888 at the top — which is genuinely useful budget framing, and he proactively offered to log the unit numbers so the booking would be one step when she called back.
coaching_note: Chris, the highest-leverage fix is the three differentiators you skipped entirely — No Worries, Meet Your Mover, On-Time Guarantee. You said 'insurance' is included and moved on. Say it in full instead: 'Insurance is included, and that's our No Worries Damage Coverage — up to $2,000 per move to repair, replace, or reimburse any accidental damage. A few days before your move we'll email you your mover's photo and info so you know exactly who's showing up. And we run an On-Time Guarantee — if we miss your arrival window, we start discounting immediately.' That is roughly forty seconds and it is the difference between a price and a reason to pick us. Second priority: you had a warm buyer stalling on a roommate conversation and you never said 'no deposit.' The close was right there — 'There's no deposit to hold a date, so I can put Saturday the fifth on the schedule right now and you can move or cancel it free once you've talked to your roommate.' Third, and this one feeds Cameron's estimate-accuracy rock: you learned about third-floor stairs and a garage pickup and then quoted the stock one-bedroom range anyway. Say out loud what the variables do — 'a third-floor stair carry plus the garage will likely push you toward the top of that range' — and add the Save Your Ass speech, which you skipped completely. Prep before move day equals a shorter move equals a lower bill: consolidate the loose stuff, get the photos off the walls, and take a carload of small items yourself. On a stair carry that speech is worth real money to her and real accuracy to us.
